examples.ko: 이 수업은 멀티미디어 자료를 많이 써요.
examples.en: This class uses a lot of multimedia material.
The multimedia classroom has a big screen.
That company makes multimedia content.
Multimedia devices are very diverse these days.
I majored in multimedia at university.
I'm going to see a multimedia exhibition.

explain: 영상, 소리, 글을 함께 쓴 자료나 기술을 말해요. 일상 대화보다는 수업, 광고, 직업 이름 앞에서 '멀티미디어 교실', '멀티미디어 콘텐츠'처럼 붙여 쓰는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: This company makes multimedia content.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영상, 소리, 글이 섞인 내용물을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for content that mixes video, sound, and text.

phrases.en: I watch videos on a multimedia device.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영상과 소리를 함께 쓰는 기계를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for devices that handle both video and sound.

phrases.en: We watched a movie in the multimedia room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교나 도서관에서 영상 자료를 보는 방을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a room in a school or library for watching media.

explain_en: It refers to materials or technology that combine video, sound, and text. It appears less in casual talk and more as a modifier in school, ads, and job contexts, such as 멀티미디어 교실 or 멀티미디어 콘텐츠.

examples.en: This case is still a mystery.

examples.ko: 저는 밤에 미스터리 영화를 자주 봐요.
examples.en: I often watch mystery movies at night.
Solving a mystery is really fun.
There are a lot of mysteries on that island.
The mystery usually gets revealed at the end.
Mysteries are nice, but I like comedies more.

explain: '수수께끼'는 한국어 느낌이 나는 말이고 '미스터리'는 외래어예요. 장르를 말할 때는 '미스터리 영화', '미스터리 소설'처럼 앞에 붙여 써요.

phrases.en: I'm curious about the ending of mystery novels.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장르 이름으로 '미스터리'를 앞에 붙인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 'mystery' in front as a genre name.

phrases.en: This story is still a mystery.
phrases.nuance_ko: '미스터리'와 비슷하지만 한국어 느낌이 나는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 'mystery' but a native Korean word.

phrases.example: 미스터리한 이야기를 들으면 잠이 안 와요.
phrases.en: When I hear a mysterious story, I can't sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: '미스터리한'으로 뒤에 오는 말을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Misteorihan' describes the noun that follows.

explain_en: '수수께끼' is the native Korean word and '미스터리' is a loanword. For genres, put it in front: '미스터리 영화', '미스터리 소설'.

examples.en: When I go to a bookstore, I look at the new releases section first.
A new book by my favorite writer came out today.
I'll check whether new books have come into the library.

examples.ko: 이번 달 신간 중에서 하나를 골랐어요.
examples.en: I picked one from this month's new releases.

examples.ko: 신간은 보통 책값이 조금 더 비싸요.
examples.en: New books are usually a bit more expensive.
I gave my friend a newly published novel as a gift.

explain: 신간은 새로 나온 책이에요. 영화나 음악의 새 작품은 '신작'이라고 해서 책에만 써요. 서점에서는 오래전에 나온 책을 '구간'이라고도 하지만, 일상에서는 '예전에 나온 책'이라고 말해요.

phrases.en: Many new books arrived at the library.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서점이나 도서관 안내에서 자주 보이는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in bookstore and library notices.

phrases.example: 다음 달에 그 작가의 신간이 나와요.
phrases.en: That author's new book comes out next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 책이 출판될 때 '나오다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 나오다 when a new book is published.

phrases.example: 이번 신간 소설을 꼭 사고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I really want to buy this new novel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책 종류를 붙여 어떤 새 책인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add the book type to say what kind of new release.

explain_en: 신간 is a newly published book. A new film or album is called '신작', so 신간 is used only for books. Bookstores sometimes call older titles '구간', but in daily speech people say '예전에 나온 책'.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 본명은 예명과 완전히 달라요.
examples.en: That singer's real name is completely different from the stage name.
I use a stage name when I sing.
The stage name is far more famous than the real name.
The singer performs under a stage name, so I don't know the real name.
I was curious what the stage name meant, so I looked up an interview.
Can I call you by your real name instead of your stage name?

explain: 가수나 배우가 활동할 때 쓰는 이름이에요. 짝이 되는 말은 '본명'이고, 글 쓰는 사람이 쓰는 이름은 '필명'이라고 해서 구분해요.

phrases.en: The singer came up with the stage name herself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 활동 이름을 만들 때 '짓다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 짓다 when someone creates a new name to perform under.
phrases.en_equiv: to come up with a stage name

phrases.en: That actor works under a stage name.
phrases.nuance_ko: 본명 대신 다른 이름으로 일한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means working under a different name instead of one's real name.
phrases.en_equiv: to work under a stage name

phrases.example: 그 가수의 본명은 많이 알려지지 않았어요.
phrases.en: That singer's real name isn't widely known.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예명과 짝이 되는 말로, 태어날 때 받은 진짜 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The counterpart of 예명: the real name a person was given at birth.

explain_en: It is the name a singer or actor uses while performing. Its counterpart is '본명' (real name), and the name a writer uses is called '필명' (pen name).

en: to be edited; to be compiled

examples.en: The video was edited nicely.
The interview is edited to fit the length.

examples.ko: 사진이 너무 많이 편집된 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think the photo has been edited too much.

examples.ko: 이 책은 여러 사람의 글이 모여 편집되었어요.
examples.en: This book was compiled from the writings of several people.
Unnecessary parts are cut out and the broadcast comes out.
When the file is edited, it is saved automatically.

explain: 영상·사진·글·책을 다듬고 정리해서 하나로 만든다는 뜻이에요. 글을 고치는 '수정하다'보다 전체 구성과 순서를 손보는 느낌이 강해요. 하는 사람은 '편집하다', 일을 하는 사람은 '편집자'예요.

phrases.en: This video is well edited.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '편집'과 함께 결과가 좋다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 편집 to say the editing turned out well.

phrases.en: My friend edited my video for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하는 사람이 주어일 때 쓰는 능동형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, with the person doing the editing as the subject.

phrases.en: The editor read my writing and corrected it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 편집하는 일을 하는 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a person whose job is editing.

explain_en: It covers tidying and arranging video, photos, text or books into one finished piece. Compared with 수정하다 (fix), it feels more about the overall structure and order. The doer's verb is 편집하다 and the professional is a 편집자 (editor).

examples.en: This film is a joint work of Korea and France.

examples.ko: 그 노래는 두 가수의 합작품이라서 더 특별해요.
examples.en: That song is a collaboration of two singers, so it's more special.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 여러 건축가의 합작품으로 알려져 있어요.
examples.en: This building is known as the joint work of several architects.
The finished cake was a joint effort of the whole family.
For a joint work, the quality is really high.

examples.ko: 합작품은 의견을 맞추는 과정이 힘들 수 있어요.
examples.en: With a joint work, the process of matching opinions can be hard.

explain: 영화·드라마·음악처럼 두 나라나 두 사람 이상이 함께 만든 작품에 써요. 가볍게는 '우리 가족의 합작품'처럼 여럿이 힘을 모아 이룬 결과물에도 써요. '공동 작품'이라고 풀어서 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 이 그림은 우리 반의 공동 작품이에요.
phrases.en: This painting is a joint work of our class.
phrases.nuance_ko: '합작품'을 풀어서 말한 표현이라 더 쉽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain-language way of saying the headword, so it sounds easier.

phrases.example: 그 합작 영화는 두 나라에서 인기를 끌었어요.
phrases.en: That co-produced film was popular in both countries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 나라 이상이 함께 만든 영화를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a film made together by two or more countries.

phrases.en: This cake is a joint effort of my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여럿이 힘을 모아 만든 결과물을 가볍게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used lightly for something made by combining everyone's effort.

explain_en: It is used for works such as films, dramas and music made together by two countries or two or more people. In a lighter way, it also fits results many people made together, like '우리 가족의 합작품'. People sometimes say '공동 작품' instead.

examples.en: I rode the carousel at the amusement park.
The kids say they like the carousel best.
The carousel turns slowly, so it isn't scary.

examples.ko: 회전목마 앞에 줄이 길게 서 있어요.
examples.en: There is a long line in front of the carousel.

examples.ko: 회전목마에서 내리자마자 또 타고 싶다고 했어요.
examples.en: As soon as she got off the carousel, she said she wanted another ride.
At night the lights come on at the carousel and it looks pretty.

explain: 놀이공원에서 가장 순한 놀이기구를 말할 때 자주 나와요. 무서운 놀이기구는 '롤러코스터'나 '바이킹'이라고 하고, 회전목마는 어린아이도 탈 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I rode the carousel with my younger sibling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀이기구를 탄다고 할 때 가장 기본으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to say you rode the attraction.

phrases.en: The carousel turns to the music.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회전목마가 움직이는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes the carousel in motion.

phrases.en: Let's meet in front of the carousel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀이공원에서 만날 장소를 정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Handy for picking a meeting spot in an amusement park.

explain_en: 회전목마 comes up as the gentlest ride at an amusement park. Scary rides are called 롤러코스터 or 바이킹, while even small children can ride a 회전목마.

examples.en: I caught a crayfish in the stream.
Crayfish only live in clean water.

examples.ko: 아이들이 돌 밑에 숨은 가재를 찾았어요.
examples.en: The children found a crayfish hiding under a rock.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 시골 계곡에서 가재 잡는 게 제일 재미있었어요.
examples.en: As a kid, catching crayfish in the country valley was the most fun.

examples.ko: 가재 두 마리가 어항 안에 있어요.
examples.en: There are two crayfish in the fish tank.
This crayfish has really big claws.

explain: 한국에서 가재는 보통 맑은 계곡이나 개울에서 잡는 작은 민물 동물이에요. 바다의 큰 '바닷가재'(랍스터)와 달라서, 요리 재료를 말할 때는 '바닷가재'라고 해야 해요.

phrases.example: 가재는 게 편이라고, 두 사람이 서로 감싸 주네요.
phrases.en: People in similar situations take each other's side.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처지나 모양이 비슷한 사람끼리 서로 편들어 준다는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning that people in similar situations side with each other.
phrases.en_equiv: Birds of a feather flock together

explain_en: In Korea 가재 usually means the small freshwater animal caught in clean streams and valleys. It is different from the big sea '바닷가재' (lobster), so for cooking ingredients you must say '바닷가재'.

examples.en: They say the universe is infinitely wide.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 인기는 무한히 이어질 것 같아요.
examples.en: That singer's popularity seems like it will last without end.
A mother's love is limitlessly deep.
The possibilities are open without limit.

examples.ko: 우리에게 시간이 무한히 있는 것은 아니에요.
examples.en: We don't have unlimited time.

examples.ko: 아이는 같은 노래를 무한히 반복해서 들었어요.
examples.en: The child listened to the same song on endless repeat.

explain: '무한히'는 '끝없이'와 비슷하지만 더 딱딱한 글말이에요. 대화에서는 '끝없이'나 '한없이'를 더 많이 쓰고, 무한히는 수학이나 과학, 연설처럼 크게 말할 때 어울려요. '무한하다'의 반대는 '유한하다'예요.

phrases.en: The sea stretches out endlessly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무한히'와 뜻은 비슷하지만 대화에서 더 자연스럽고 부드러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means about the same as 'muhanhi' but sounds softer and more natural in conversation.

phrases.en: I feel endlessly happy when I look at my child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감정이 끝도 없이 크다고 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: It fits well when a feeling is so big it seems to have no limit.

phrases.example: 그 숫자는 무한히 커질 수 있어요.
phrases.en: That number can grow infinitely large.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수학이나 과학처럼 딱딱한 설명에서 '무한히' 뒤에 자주 붙는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in stiff explanations such as math or science.

explain_en: 무한히 is close to 끝없이 but stiffer and more bookish. In conversation, 끝없이 and 한없이 are used more, and 무한히 fits math, science and speeches where things are described on a grand scale. The opposite of 무한하다 is 유한하다.

examples.en: The spring breeze is blowing softly. Want to take a walk together?
The puppy ran over wagging its tail.
I like the sound of leaves rustling lightly in the wind.

examples.ko: 커튼이 살랑거려서 창문이 열린 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: The curtain was swaying, so I thought the window was open.

examples.ko: 치마 끝이 살랑거릴 때마다 기분이 좋아요.
examples.en: I feel happy every time the hem of my skirt sways.
The blades of grass swayed gently all afternoon.

explain: 바람, 꼬리, 잎처럼 가벼운 것이 부드럽게 흔들릴 때 써요. '살랑대다', '살랑이다'도 비슷한 뜻이고, 일상에서는 '살랑살랑 불다, 흔들다'로도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: The gently blowing breeze feels cool.
phrases.nuance_ko: '살랑거리는' 뒤에 바람을 붙여 부드러운 바람을 꾸며 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '살랑거리는' placed before 'wind' describes a soft breeze.

phrases.en: The leaves are swaying lightly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '살랑거리다'와 같은 뜻이고 조금 더 짧게 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '살랑거리다', just a bit shorter.

phrases.en: A soft breeze is blowing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람이 약하고 부드럽게 부는 모습을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for a weak, soft breeze.

explain_en: Use it when something light, like the wind, a tail or leaves, moves softly. '살랑대다' and '살랑이다' mean about the same, and in daily speech people also say '살랑살랑 불다' or '흔들다'.

t90.ax: The puppy ran over wagging its tail.

examples.en: I made a bouquet by adding baby's breath to the roses.

examples.ko: 안개꽃은 작고 하얀 꽃이 많이 피어요.
examples.en: Baby's breath blooms with many small white flowers.
I put a bunch of baby's breath in a vase.

examples.ko: 안개꽃이 있으니 꽃다발이 더 풍성해 보여요.
examples.en: With the baby's breath, the bouquet looks fuller.
I tried decorating my room with baby's breath.
I dry baby's breath and use it as decoration.

explain: 장미 같은 큰 꽃 사이에 채워 넣는 꽃으로 꽃다발이나 꽃꽂이에서 자주 보여요. 작은 꽃이 구름이나 안개처럼 퍼져 보이는 모습이 특징이에요. 말려서 드라이플라워로 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: I received a bouquet of baby's breath as a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안개꽃으로 만든 꽃다발을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for a bouquet made of gypsophila.

phrases.en: Baby's breath has bloomed in the flower bed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃이 필 때 쓰는 기본 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic phrase for flowers blooming.

phrases.en: I dried the baby's breath and used it as decoration.
phrases.nuance_ko: 드라이플라워로 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when making dried flowers.

explain_en: It is a flower often tucked between bigger flowers like roses in bouquets and arrangements. Its small blooms spread out like a cloud or mist. People also dry it and use it as a dried flower.

examples.ko: 이 강에는 작은 지류가 여러 개 있어요.
examples.en: This river has several small tributaries.
A tributary flows into a big river.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 오면 지류의 물이 먼저 불어요.
examples.en: When it rains a lot, the water in the tributaries rises first.
Find the tributaries of the Han River on the map.

examples.ko: 마을은 두 지류가 만나는 곳에 있어요.
examples.en: The village is where two tributaries meet.
In this tributary, water flows only in summer.

explain: 반대말은 '본류'예요. 큰 강으로 흘러 들어가는 작은 물줄기이고, 같은 말로 '지천'도 써요. 일상 대화보다 지리 수업이나 지도 설명에서 나와요.

phrases.example: 이 마을은 강의 지류 옆에 있어요.
phrases.en: This village is next to a tributary of the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어느 큰 강에 속한 작은 물줄기를 말할 때 이렇게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to name a small stream that belongs to a big river.

phrases.en: I tried telling the main stream and tributaries apart on the map.
phrases.nuance_ko: '본류'는 큰 줄기이고 '지류'는 거기로 흘러드는 작은 줄기예요. 둘을 함께 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '본류' is the main stream and '지류' flows into it. The two are often said together.

phrases.en: That stream flows into the Han River.
phrases.nuance_ko: '지류'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 큰 강으로 흘러드는 작은 하천을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as '지류'. Used for a small stream that flows into a big river.

explain_en: The opposite is 본류. It is a small stream that flows into a bigger river, and 지천 means the same. It comes up in geography lessons and map descriptions more than in daily talk.

examples.en: Everest is known as the highest peak in the world.
Hallasan is the highest peak in South Korea.
I met a writer who reached the pinnacle of literature.

examples.ko: 등산객들이 최고봉을 향해 한 걸음씩 올라갔어요.
examples.en: The hikers climbed step by step toward the highest peak.

examples.ko: 최고봉은 눈이 덮여 있어서 오르기 어려워요.
examples.en: The highest peak is covered with snow, so it is hard to climb.

examples.ko: 이 작품은 그의 예술에서 최고봉의 위치를 차지해요.
examples.en: This work holds the pinnacle position in his art.

explain: 산에서는 가장 높은 봉우리를, 일이나 분야에서는 가장 뛰어난 수준을 비유로 말해요. '최고봉에 오르다', '~의 최고봉'처럼 써요. 그냥 '최고'라고 해도 되지만, 최고봉은 높은 산을 올랐다는 무게 있는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.example: 이 작품은 한국 영화의 최고봉으로 꼽혀요.
phrases.en: This work is ranked as the pinnacle of Korean film.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분야 이름 뒤에 붙여 가장 뛰어난 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attached after a field to mean the best of it.

phrases.en: He reached the top of the cooking world.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 높은 수준에 이르렀다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means reaching the highest level.

phrases.example: 이 산의 최고봉까지 세 시간 걸려요.
phrases.en: It takes three hours to reach this mountain's highest peak.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 산의 가장 높은 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the real highest point of a mountain.
phrases.en_equiv: the highest peak of a mountain

explain_en: On a mountain it names the highest peak, and for work or a field it figuratively names the top level. It appears as 최고봉에 오르다 and '~의 최고봉'. Plain 최고 also works, but 최고봉 carries a weighty feel of having climbed a high mountain.

examples.en: The government reforms the education system.
They picked a new head to reform the company.
We reformed the old way, and work got faster.
After the reform, the students liked it.
I want to reform this rule.
We have to decide what to reform first.

explain: 제도, 조직, 규칙 같은 큰 것을 근본부터 바꾼다는 말이에요. 작은 물건이나 습관은 '고치다', '바꾸다'를 써요. 뉴스에서는 '개혁'이라는 명사 모양으로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I want to reform this system.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 싶다'를 붙여 바람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '-고 싶다' to express a wish.

phrases.en: We need to reform the old rules.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어야 하다'로 꼭 필요하다는 뜻을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-아/어야 하다' says it is necessary.

phrases.en: The school changed its old rules.
phrases.nuance_ko: '개혁하다'보다 쉽고 일상적이며, 큰 일과 작은 일에 모두 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and more everyday than '개혁하다', usable for big and small things.

explain_en: It means changing something big, such as a system, organization or rule, from its foundations. For small objects or habits use '고치다' or '바꾸다'. In the news it often appears as the noun '개혁'.

examples.en: France is a republic without a king.
In a republic, an elected person leads the country.
India became a republic in 1950.
People gathered to found a new republic.
Korea is also a republic, so we elect a president.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 로마 공화국에 대해 배웠어요.
examples.en: We learned about the Roman Republic in history class.

explain: '공화국'은 나라 이름이나 정치 제도를 말할 때 나와요. '대한민국은 민주공화국이다'라는 문장이 헌법에도 있어요. 짝이 되는 말로 '왕국'을 써요.

phrases.en: The Republic of Korea is a democratic republic.
phrases.nuance_ko: '공화국' 앞에 '민주'가 붙은 말로, 헌법에도 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: 공화국 with 민주 in front; it appears in the constitution.

phrases.en: The UK is a kingdom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 왕이 있는 나라로, '공화국'과 짝이 되는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A country with a king; the counterpart of 공화국.

phrases.en: Citizens of a republic can vote.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '의'를 붙여 공화국에 속한 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 의 to refer to people who belong to a republic.

explain_en: It appears in country names and when talking about political systems. The sentence '대한민국은 민주공화국이다' is in the constitution. The contrasting word is '왕국' (kingdom).
